headline: This law lets the HUD Secretary add or change rules for federally insured reverse mortgages to strengthen the program's finances.
what_it_does: It changes the National Housing Act so HUD can set new or different requirements for home equity conversion mortgages, which are reverse mortgages for older homeowners. HUD can make these changes by notice or mortgagee letter instead of going through a longer process. The new requirements take effect as soon as HUD issues them.

who_it_affects.group: Homeowners aged 62 and older with reverse mortgages
who_it_affects.how: HUD can change the rules for these loans, which may affect the terms they get or keep.

who_it_affects.group: Lenders that offer federally insured reverse mortgages
who_it_affects.how: They must follow any new or changed requirements HUD issues for the program.
The rules they face may change over time as HUD issues new requirements.

when_it_takes_effect: Each new requirement takes effect when HUD issues it. The law itself was enacted on August 9, 2013.
